title: Children's Librarian Volunteer
transcript:
Speaker 0: HEAD LIBRARIAN: Good morning. You’d like to volunteer for the children’s section. Is that right?
Speaker 2: TESSA: Yes. I spoke to you on the phone yesterday.
Speaker 0: HEAD LIBRARIAN: That’s right. Tessa, isn’t it? Yes. Tessa Bridges. Thank you for coming in today, Tessa. Before we discuss what a volunteer does in the library, I’ll need to get some details from you.
Speaker 2: TESSA: No problem. What would you like
Speaker 0: HEAD LIBRARIAN: to know? Where do you live, Tessa?
Speaker 2: TESSA: I still live with my family in Northwood. 51 Matthew Drive.
Speaker 0: HEAD LIBRARIAN: M A T H E W, Mathew Drive.
Speaker 2: TESSA: Actually, there are two t’s, m a, double t, h e w.
Speaker 0: HEAD LIBRARIAN: Oh, thank you. And the postcode for Northwood is?
Speaker 2: TESSA: Oh, I’m still confused about that. It used to be 2614, which, of course, I still remember, but the post office has recently changed it to 4126.
Speaker 0: HEAD LIBRARIAN: So 4126. Now you’re a university student, aren’t you?
Speaker 2: TESSA: Not exactly. I go to Northwood Polytechnic. I’m in my final year.
Speaker 0: HEAD LIBRARIAN: In your final year. So what are you studying? I mean, your main subject.
Speaker 2: TESSA: Oh, I’m majoring in creative writing.
Speaker 0: HEAD LIBRARIAN: And are you enjoying that?
Speaker 2: TESSA: Very much so. I love it. When I graduate, I want to write children’s books.
Speaker 0: HEAD LIBRARIAN: That’s great. Now I can see why you’re keen to volunteer at the library. We’re always grateful for the extra help, but I still have to ask you some more questions about your previous experience.
Speaker 2: TESSA: That’s fine. But I haven’t had a full time paid job yet.
Speaker 0: HEAD LIBRARIAN: Not to worry. Part time work or voluntary work gives you the experience most employers are looking for.
Speaker 2: TESSA: Well, to start with, when I was 16, I had a babysitting job.
Speaker 0: HEAD LIBRARIAN: And who did you work for?
Speaker 2: TESSA: Oh, just family friends.
Speaker 0: HEAD LIBRARIAN: How long did you babysit for family friends? Oh, about two years, on and off. After those two years were up, what did you do then?
Speaker 2: TESSA: Well, I was still working as a babysitter on the occasional evening and weekend when I became a peer tutor at school. I did that for one year, my last year at senior high.
Speaker 0: HEAD LIBRARIAN: And what does being a peer tutor involve?
Speaker 2: TESSA: Mostly, it means staying behind after school one or two afternoons a week to help fellow students in the subject that they’re having difficulty with.
Speaker 0: HEAD LIBRARIAN: And what subject did you tutor in?
Speaker 2: TESSA: English, actually.
Speaker 0: HEAD LIBRARIAN: I see. Do you have any other experience?
Speaker 2: TESSA: I worked at the Ace Sports Academy as a tennis coach, but that was only for about twelve weeks over the summer before I enrolled at the Polytechnic.
Speaker 0: HEAD LIBRARIAN: So you’re good at sports? Not everything. Just tennis. And are you currently working?
Speaker 2: TESSA: Yes. Well, unpaid work, that is. I’m a volunteer at the local hospital where I visit sick children who would otherwise not have any visitors.
Speaker 0: HEAD LIBRARIAN: Well, it certainly seems as if you like children.
Speaker 2: TESSA: Yes. I do.
Speaker 0: HEAD LIBRARIAN: Well, Tessa, what I need to know now is what your schedule is like so that we can fit you into the roster here. Can I assume that you’re not able to work Monday to Friday during office hours?
Speaker 2: TESSA: Right. I’m very busy with lectures, workshops, and assignments during the week.
Speaker 0: HEAD LIBRARIAN: How about weeknights? Say five to seven in the evening. That’s a very busy time in the children’s section.
Speaker 2: TESSA: Well, I couldn’t commit to more than three evenings a week. And even then, it would depend on my schedule.
Speaker 0: HEAD LIBRARIAN: Yes.
I understand.
Speaker 0: If possible, we could make arrangements a week in advance. Would that help? Yes. That might work. Are weekends okay?
Speaker 2: TESSA: Well, Sundays are out. Actually, only every other Sunday because that’s when I’m usually needed at the hospital. But I’m free on Saturday afternoons.
Speaker 0: HEAD LIBRARIAN: Alright. We could roster you for the odd weekend then. What about school holidays?
Speaker 2: TESSA: Definitely. No problem whatsoever. I don’t have any other commitments during the holidays.
Speaker 0: HEAD LIBRARIAN: That’s good to hear. We have droves of children here in the holidays as you can imagine. Thank you. Well, Tessa, we’ll send you a letter of appointment in the mail, and we look forward to having you join us as a volunteer.
Speaker 2: TESSA: Thanks very much.
Speaker 0: HEAD LIBRARIAN: Now as for your duties That is the end of part one. You now have one minute to check your answers to part one.
